title: Only One Lazio Star Made Mancini's November Squad, And Italy's Quarter-Final Fate Rides On It - NewsBreak
text:
By Daniel Worbowski ,
4 hours ago
Soccer on gradient background — Created by the Sports On Tap desk | Source : Sports On Tap (team logos property of their respective owners)
Roberto Mancini, Italy’s head coach, has officially named his 31-player squad for the upcoming November international break, and only one Lazio player made the cut: midfielder Davide Frattesi.
Zaccagni’s Injury Leaves A Void, Mussolini Snubbed
Frattesi’s inclusion itself isn’t a shocker. The 27-year-old Roman kept his spot from the September-October international break, where he was heavily involved and even considered among Italy’s top performers. Even with a slight dip in his form after a sensational start to his Lazio stint, his recall was hardly a surprise.
The real story, though, is who *isn’t* joining him from the club. Lazio captain Mattia Zaccagni, who was in fine form, got sidelined by a muscle injury during Sunday’s win over Cagliari. That’s a huge blow, potentially keeping him out for a month. And Romano Floriani Mussolini? He was on Mancini’s shortlist, a rising star, but ultimately got snubbed. So yeah, it’s just Frattesi from the blue and white.
Quarter-Final Dreams Hinge On France and Belgium
Mancini isn’t shy about looking to the future either, bringing in some fresh blood. The 31-man squad features exciting young talents like 17-year-old Como midfielder Riccardo Cassano and 18-year-old Parma forward Simone Lontani. Don’t get too used to seeing them with the big boys though, they are set to rejoin Italy’s U18 and U19 squads after just a few days among the seniors.
But let’s be real, the main event for this squad is all about those two crucial UEFA Nations League group-stage fixtures. The Azzurri are hosting France at San Siro on November 12, then hitting the road to face Belgium away from home on November 15. This is it for the group stage, folks.
Italy’s got seven points from their first four outings so far, bouncing back after an opening matchday loss to Belgium. They beat Turkiye home and away, and snatched a draw against Zinedine Zidane’s side in France. To keep their quarter-final dreams alive, they absolutely need to finish either first or second in the group.
So, the stage is set. Two games, everything on the line for a quarter-final berth. Can Mancini’s somewhat surprising squad navigate these huge tests against two top-tier nations? You bet we’ll be watching every kick.
